Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Sign-in hardening: refused default secrets, failed sign-in limit, password rule, admin guard, HTTPS switch

- A server with LOUPE_ENV=production refuses to start on a missing or shipped secret, naming it. Live is not marked
  yet: its settings hold no signing key of their own. deploy/rotate-secrets.sh gives it its own secrets, moves stored
  AI credentials to the new key with no moment unreadable, and sets the mark.
- Failed sign-ins are limited from the activity trail (Postgres, so across workers), before the password hash.
  Only failures count. A plain message gives the wait; a refusal is audited once a minute.
- New passwords on every path: 12 characters, not common, not the person's own name.
- Admin screens show non-admins a plain refused page on the first paint. Someone else's background tasks are for
  administrators.
- LOUPE_HTTPS (off) sets the Secure cookie flag and HSTS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Brokerage rows: release review fixes (statements re-read, removed or restored; corrected values; fund money direction; holdings per account)

- A re-read statement is saved before the copy it replaces is set aside: rows are unique per statement and printed
  line (not per file), so the new reading's trades and holdings are written instead of failing on the old ones.
- A file of several statements: each statement's holdings come from its own recorded pages only.
- A row counts only while its statement is in the ledger (not removed, set aside or replaced); the lists say how many
  are not shown. Set-aside, restore and removal now re-sync the statement's rows.
- A correction is the value in effect in the row itself, so searches, date filters, sorting and sums use it; the
  value as read stays in the correction; a confirmation is held against the reading as read.
- Fund trades carry the investor's money direction (a sale is money received; a reclassification is neither).
- Holdings totals are per account, instrument and kind, summed over every line of the latest date.
- A statement's computed proof class is carried as is (p4 is no longer raised to p3).
- A citation link opens the cited row (GET /security-rows/{id}) wherever it falls, in its own kind, with whether it
  counts.
- Paging order ends on the row id (total order); a corrected number must be a number (no decimal comma), compared
  as a number.

Each fix has a test that fails on the code before it (6 tests).

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Give the localisation arithmetic a reader, and say when a quarantine balances the statement

The quarantine arithmetic was complete and unreachable. localise, would_rescue
and QuarantineBasis.from_proof all worked, and all of them took hand-built
observations, so nothing in the running system could ask them anything.
services/financial/localisation.py is the join: stored rows to observations, a
stored period to a live identity outcome, and the two rescue questions asked of
a real ledger.

Two decisions in that module are load bearing and are documented where they are
made. The chain is walked over admitted rows only, because localise calls a set
of breaks proved when they account for the whole residual, and the residual
comes from total_transactions, which sums admitted rows; walking any other
population against that residual compares two numbers that do not measure the
same thing, and proved is the one verdict here that is grounds for setting
evidence aside. And the identity is recomputed rather than read off the period,
because the column holds whatever the last reconciliation wrote and the rescue
question is about the gap as it stands at the moment of the write.

The hazard this exists to surface: removing a row whose amount equals the gap
makes the statement balance by arithmetic necessity, whatever the row was. So
quarantine_case_row now asks the question before the mutation, while the row is
still admitted and the period's totals still contain it, and reports the answer
on the adjudication. It refuses nothing. A row proved wrong by its own
statement should come out and the statement should then balance; what a reviewer
needs is not a verdict but the fact that the balance was reached by subtraction,
sitting next to the grounds so the two can be weighed together.

rescues_period is three-valued on purpose. True is a finding, False is the
opposite finding, and None means the question could not be answered because
computing the identity raised. The three cover different things and flattening
them would let a period nobody could check read as a period checked and found
safe. A period that already balanced, one whose statement printed no balances,
and a row in no period at all are all False: where there is no gap, no gap was
closed.

The sentence describing the rescue travels in the response, not in the reason
handed to QuarantineBasis.from_adjudication. That method builds its detail as
"<person>: <their reason>" and that detail is what the adjudication log stores,
so anything appended would leave a record in which a person appears to have
written words the system wrote. Giving the fact a durable home in the log needs
somewhere that is neither the person's reason nor the row's before/after
columns, which is a change to quarantine_transaction and is not made here.

The adjudication route returns as_dict() unchanged, so the finding reaches the
interface with no schema work; its test now asserts that rather than assuming it.

Suite 3300 to 3336, all passing.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Record adjudications as events, not as columns on the thing decided

A disposition written only onto the row it concerns cannot survive its own
reversal.  restore_document nulls both superseded_by_id and
duplicate_match_rung -- correctly, a restored document is not a duplicate --
so afterwards it is byte-identical to one that was never excluded, and the
exclusion, its rung, its reason and its author are gone.  Releasing a
quarantined row has the same shape: ck_financial_transactions_quarantine_coherent
requires a released row to carry a null reason, so the reason for the
original quarantine has nowhere to live.  In both cases the history is not
merely hard to query, it is absent.

services/financial/decisions.py appends instead.  Every disposition now
writes an event carrying actor, reason, before and after, and every reversal
is its own appended event rather than a retraction, which is why
AdjudicationDecision pairs each disposition with its undo.

subject_sequence is what orders them.  created_at cannot: Postgres now() is
transaction-start time, so a supersession and the restore that undid it --
the pair that most needs ordering -- share it, and breaking the tie on a
uuid4 id is a coin toss that reads as authoritative.

Two defects surfaced from the tests rather than from reasoning:

  resolve_duplicates is re-runnable and reached _supersede on already
  superseded documents, appending an identical before/after each time.  The
  log would then have answered "how often was this excluded" with the number
  of times the resolver was run.  The event is now conditional on the
  snapshots differing; the row-hiding update is not, because a row ingested
  after the supersession still needs hiding, and that is reconciling state
  rather than taking a decision.

  decision was free text while subject_type was constrained, which is the
  wrong way round -- the subject is a table name only this codebase writes,
  the decision is what a deposition asks and a GROUP BY answers.  This file
  had itself written 'admit', 'supersede' and 'quarantine' for what are three
  of the six admitted values.  Closing the vocabulary caught all three.

The ledger's own structural guard caught the follow-on: a new closed
vocabulary was on the model but unregistered in VOCABULARY_CONSTRAINTS, so
nothing was checking the constraint against the enum member for member.

Three fixture tests were passing on an unrelated NOT NULL rather than the
constraints they named, and are now assertRejectedBy.  The history ordering
test was passing under a created_at ordering too, because rows written in
one second come back in insertion order; it now backdates the reversal so
the two orderings actively disagree.  16/16 mutations caught, 640 tests.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Check row dates against what can be proved, not against a guess

Dates decide ordering, period membership and every "what happened between
X and Y" answer the system gives, and the year is four glyphs that OCR
treats as unremarkable. This adds the check between a date as extracted
and a date the ledger acts on.

The design is measured rather than assumed. Across 30,570 rows in 325
corpus documents, every date parses, exactly one row is provably wrong,
and 343 rows fall outside their document's stated period. Those two facts
point in opposite directions and keeping them apart is the whole job.

The one provable row postdates the moment its own document was read, so
the contradiction needs no invented constant: a statement cannot print a
transaction that has not happened. There is therefore no minimum year, no
maximum age and no configurable window, because those are guesses and a
guess that quarantines evidence is worse than no check. The corpus holds
no implausibly old row, so no rule is invented to catch one.

Being outside the stated period proves nothing about the row. 332 of the
343 sit in one 180-page file whose rows span 47 months under a period
stating 18; the rows are almost certainly right and the period is almost
certainly a misread aggregate. Acting on that signal would discard good
evidence to protect a worse field, and would do so hardest exactly where
the document was hardest to read. So DateFinding.grounds() refuses to
produce a quarantine basis from it, and says why.

What the pair does prove is a contradiction without a culprit: if the
rows span more calendar time than the period provides, no assignment of
blame to individual dates reconciles them. That is a proof rather than a
threshold, needs no tuning, and catches all four corpus documents,
including the one exceeding its period by a single day — ratios run 12.93,
2.63, 1.16 and 1.01, and no percentage separates the last from an
ordinary document.

A derived bound cannot check the rows it came from. The corpus proves it:
the 2321 row's document has period end 2321-10-08 because the bound was
taken from the maximum row date and inherited the defect. Comparison is
refused unless both bounds were printed, as PeriodBounds.supports_-
continuity already requires, and the refusal is recorded as its own
outcome because "not checked" and "checked and fine" are different states
and only one is reassuring.

observed_at has no default. A finding that changes with the day it was
computed cannot be reproduced from the record.

Verified against the corpus itself: the module independently reproduces
the measurement — 1 impossible row, 343 refusals of grounds, and the same
four span contradictions with identical spans. 35 tests, mutation-verified
against nine removals including grounds-from-out-of-period, period-before-
impossibility, disproved-rows-in-span, threshold-instead-of-proof and
read_row_date reaching for the wrong column. 550 backend tests pass.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
financial: localise a failing balance identity, and require grounds to quarantine

When the identity fails, "this statement does not balance by 50.00" is not
yet a finding. services.financial.quarantine narrows it: it walks the
statement's own printed running balances and names the first row where the
chain breaks, which is a proof about a specific row rather than a claim
about the document.

The design is set by what the corpus actually supports. Against the twelve
documents whose identity fails for no recorded reason, matching a single row
to the residual returns nothing nine times out of twelve; two have exactly
one row equal to the residual, and one has an eight-way tie because the
residual is 20.00 and 20.00 is a common amount. Subset search makes this
worse rather than better -- pairs and triples leave the same nine at zero
while the ambiguous document climbs from three candidates to twenty. So
there is no subset search here, and a candidate is never grounds.

That last point is enforced by construction rather than by convention.
Quarantine removes a row from every total, so quarantining the row whose
amount equals the residual makes the period balance by arithmetic necessity
-- and does so most confidently where the coincidence is most ordinary.
QuarantineBasis therefore has no constructor that accepts a Candidate:
grounds are a proved break in the chain, or a person who put their name to
the decision, and nothing else. would_rescue records, before the write, when
a quarantine would turn a failing period into a passing one, because the
difference between removing bad evidence and removing inconvenient evidence
is visible in the grounds and not in the arithmetic.

Unlocalised is the ordinary answer, so LocalisationStrength.none is a result
and not an error. The nine documents this cannot localise are all missing
the same thing: a printed running balance. 30,570 rows across 325 documents
and not one running-balance column. The chain walk is implemented anyway,
because camt.053, BAI2 and MT940 all carry balances -- which makes those
nine an argument for the native parsers rather than for a cleverer search.

The status and the reason are now held to agree by the database, in both
directions, on rows and on documents. A row marked quarantined with no
reason has been removed from every total on grounds nobody recorded; a
reason left behind on an admitted row describes a decision that was
reversed and cannot be told from one still standing. The reasons are a
closed vocabulary for the same reason every other vocabulary here is:
"balance break", "balance_break" and "broke the chain" are three answers to
a question that has one. The migration refuses to run against rows that
already violate either rule, naming them rather than letting Postgres name
a constraint.

Two things the coherence constraint caught, both worth recording. Existing
test helpers were fabricating rows quarantined on no grounds at all; the
services were checked first, and only the fixtures were wrong. And a new
document-level test was passing on a unique-key collision rather than on
the rule it named -- assertRejectedBy now asserts which constraint did the
refusing, because "some integrity error occurred" is not the assertion
anyone meant to write.

474 financial tests pass. Single alembic head at 20260830_quarantine_reasons.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Record what produced each fact in the financial ledger

Every source document, statement period and transaction already carries a
non-null ingestion_run_id, so the database refuses an unattributed fact.
What the database cannot do is make the run tell the truth about itself.
That comes down to two promises, and the tests are mostly about the second:

  - A run always reaches a terminal state.  The context manager records
    completed, aborted or failed on every exit path including
    KeyboardInterrupt, and reap_stale_runs covers the one case no in-process
    handler can — a process killed outright.  A row left saying 'running'
    is worse than no row, because it reads as work still in progress.

  - A failed run still leaves a record.  The bookkeeping uses a session of
    its own, so the rollback that discards a failed run's partial data does
    not also discard the evidence that the run ever happened.  Sharing the
    caller's session would turn a recorded failure into a silent gap, and
    silent gaps are the specific thing this subsystem exists to prevent.

code_version is derived rather than declared.  A hand-maintained constant
answers "what did someone remember to type", which is not evidence of
anything; a sha256 over the package's own source answers "what code read
this statement", and it can be recomputed by anyone holding the same tree.
There was no version constant anywhere in the backend to read, so nothing
was given up by measuring instead.  The cost is honest churn: editing a
comment moves the fingerprint, because the fingerprint is over bytes.  That
is the correct trade — a version that only moves when someone decides it
should is exactly the version that is stale when it matters.  Source that
cannot be read records '1.0.0+unverified' rather than a bare version,
because a field that is sometimes a measurement and sometimes a guess is
worse than one that says which it is.

ruleset_version is a sha256 over canonical JSON, and refuses a
non-serialisable ruleset rather than coercing it: a coerced rule is one
whose recorded version no longer identifies it.  None in gives None out,
recording that no ruleset was in force rather than inventing a version for
an absence.

stamp() checks attribution rather than merely performing it.  A row with no
ingestion_run_id is refused rather than silently skipped, because the caller
believed it was recording provenance and the whole value of the call is that
the belief is checked.  A row already belonging to another case is refused
loudly: a transaction filed under the wrong case is evidence pointed at the
wrong person.

Concurrency is deliberately not guarded.  A service-layer "is a run already
active" check would be a race rather than a protection, and claiming it as
one would be worse than the honest absence; the (source_document_id,
content_hash) uniqueness constraint is what actually stops a double count.
If concurrent runs must be prevented, that belongs in the database as a
partial unique index.

The tests run against SQLite on disk rather than in memory, because the
property under test is that two sessions are genuinely independent, and an
in-memory database gives either two empty databases or one shared
transaction — neither of which can detect the bug the design exists to
avoid.  Where SQLite's whole-file write locking shows through, the test says
so and explains what Postgres does instead.  Nine mutations of runs.py were
each killed by the test named for it.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Record whether each period value was read or inferred

A statement period has four values that can each be either a measurement or
an absence: the two dates and the two balances.  Storing them without
storing which one they are makes the whole period unusable as evidence,
because every later check has to guess.  Each now carries a source column
alongside it, and the pairing is enforced by the table rather than by
convention.

The distinction that matters most is absent from zero.  A missing opening
balance is not an opening balance of zero, and the moment those two are
stored the same way the balance identity becomes a formality that confirms
arithmetic nobody performed.  The coherence constraints compare two
booleans — (source = 'absent') = (value IS NULL) — rather than testing the
value for truthiness, because a truthiness test reads a real zero balance as
a missing one.  That is not a hypothetical: mutating the constraint to
NOT opening_balance_minor turns the suite red on exactly the test written
for it.

Period bounds get the same treatment for a different reason.  A period end
printed on the statement supports an argument about continuity; a period end
derived from the last transaction on the page does not, because it shrinks to
fit whatever was extracted.  It invents a gap whenever a month ended quietly
and closes a real one whenever the final rows were dropped — the failure the
gap detection exists to catch.  supports_continuity therefore requires both
bounds printed, and derived bounds round-trip out of the database as derived.

A carried-forward balance is not independent evidence either.  An identity
computed over one confirms consistency with the neighbouring period rather
than agreement with the source, so the row names the period it was carried
from.  That rule lives in the service layer rather than in a check
constraint on purpose: the FK cascades to NULL when a period is deleted, and
a check that a cascade can falsify would either block case deletion or leave
a surviving row violating it.  Reading a balance whose source period is gone
raises instead of quietly presenting it as intact.

Two smaller holes closed alongside.  Both Postgres and SQLite treat nulls as
distinct inside a unique constraint, so the existing constraint over
(document, account, start, end) permitted unlimited duplicate periods
whenever the dates could not be read — precisely the document hardest to
check by eye.  A partial unique index covers the undated case without
reaching onto dated rows.  And datetime is refused where a date is required,
by type identity rather than isinstance, since datetime is a date subclass
and would otherwise carry a time component into a Date column.

The migration refuses to run against a populated table rather than
backfilling.  There is no honest default: recording an existing date as
'printed' would assert that someone checked it.

45 tests, and a mutation harness covering both the service and the model,
because several of these promises are table constraints and a suite that
only exercised the service would pass against a schema permitting every
incoherent row the service declines to write.  All 22 mutations are killed
by the test named for each.

The ledger migration is re-pointed onto 20260807_deepseek, which resolves the
graph to a single head once this branch meets origin.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Detect duplicate documents by content, and exclude rather than delete

Evidence arrives with duplicates.  The same statement is disclosed twice,
or produced again in a later tranche, or scanned once and exported once.
Nothing downstream notices: each copy makes its own period rows, each set
of rows reconciles against its own printed balances, and the balance
identity is satisfied twice over.  The harm is a level up, where account
totals, the money flow view and cross-period continuity see March twice
with no way to tell that from March having happened twice.  A defect that
inflates every aggregate while every individual check passes does not
announce itself, so it has to be looked for on purpose.

Documents are fingerprinted twice, coarse and fine.  The coarse key is the
set of (account identity, period bounds, currency) signatures; the fine
one adds the sorted row hashes under each.  Both are sorted before hashing
so that neither depends on the order the database happens to return rows
in.  Matches are then graded on a nested cascade: identical bytes, then
identical reading, then merely the same accounts and periods.  The first
two justify exclusion.  The third does not -- two genuine statements can
cover the same account and month -- so it is recorded and left for a
person.

Both fingerprints are deliberately case-independent, so the same statement
filed in two matters is visible as such.  Every action taken on the
strength of a match -- exclusion, supersession, purge -- is scoped by
case_id, because cross-matter duplication is a thing to see and not a
thing to act on.

Where copies disagree, the arithmetic picks the primary: the copy that
closes against its printed balances outranks the one that does not, before
completeness, extraction layer, age or id are consulted.  Nothing is
destroyed by default.  Excluded copies are hidden and keep their rows;
purge is a separate, explicit act that records an adjudication with the
before state, so that the reason a document is gone outlives the document.

41 tests, and a mutation harness of 28 mutations each killed by the test
that names it.  Two findings from building that harness are worth the
note.  SQLite serves the period select from the unique-constraint
auto-index, so rows come back account-then-date sorted no matter how they
were inserted; within one case that order is a function of the content, so
the sort could only be exercised across two matters.  And created_at
defaults to func.now(), which has one-second resolution, so nomination
tests that left age free were decided by a second boundary roughly once in
five hundred runs.  Both are documented where they bite.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
financial: compute the balance identity per statement period

opening + (credits - debits) = closing, in integer minor units, so the
comparison is exact and the answer is yes or no rather than a score.

This is the check the extractor cannot talk its way out of.  A dropped
transaction produces no other signal: it does not arrive flagged as low
confidence, it does not arrive at all, and from the inside an extractor
that returns forty rows where the page held forty-two is
indistinguishable from one that got it right.  Confidence cannot detect
an absence.  Arithmetic can, because the absent row is still present in
the printed closing balance.  On the V1 corpus, of the 112 documents
where this identity fails, 8,544 of 8,544 rows are marked "high".

Three rules give it teeth.

It declines rather than assumes.  If either balance was not printed the
identity does not run and the period is recorded unavailable.
Substituting zero for a missing opening would manufacture a delta
exactly equal to the real opening figure, sending whoever reads it
hunting for fraud in a period whose only defect is an unreadable top of
page.  unavailable is the worse-looking answer and the more useful one.

It counts only admitted rows.  ledger_status decides what is evidence,
and the count of what was excluded travels with the result, so a period
that balances only because six rows were set aside cannot present
itself as clean.

It says whether it proved anything.  An identity struck against a
carried-forward opening is arithmetic against the neighbouring period's
closing figure, not against this statement.  It is worth computing and
it is not independent evidence.  proves_completeness is the conjunction
of balanced, independent, and complete; any one of the three missing
means the rows have not been shown to be the whole period.

Totals are summed in the database grouped by status, direction and
currency, so the row count is unbounded but the query is one.  An
admitted row in a foreign currency is refused rather than summed; a
quarantined one is merely counted, since a row that cannot reach the
total cannot corrupt it.  Totals and row counts are written even on the
unavailable path because they were genuinely computed and are useful to
whoever supplies the missing balance; what stays null is the computed
closing and the delta, which would be inventions.

Also fixes a regression this branch shipped in 0858e00.  That commit
reported 156 tests green; it was 156 of 193, because I had narrowed my
test command to three modules and dropped test_financial_ledger.  The
new period bounds source columns carry coherence constraints requiring
a bound to be 'absent' exactly when its date is null, and the ledger
fixtures neither set the columns nor registered them in the vocabulary
check.  Fixture sources are now derived from the fixture dates, so the
two cannot disagree, and the full five-module suite is 239 green.

Test suites verified by mutation rather than assumed: 21 mutations of
reconcile.py, all killed by the test named for each.  The harnesses
themselves had a defect worth recording.  CPython validates a .pyc by
comparing the source's mtime in whole seconds and its size against the
cache header.  Several mutations are byte-length identical to the code
they replace, so a restore landing in the same second as the preceding
cache write passed both halves of that check and ran the previous
iteration's bytecode against the current source -- a harness reporting
kills it had not earned.  Every run now gets a private empty
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX, and restores are verified by digest.  Re-running
the periods and runs harnesses under the fix: 22 and 9, all killed by
their named tests.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Add append-only financial ledger schema

The ledger is the system of record for financial evidence.  Six tables:
ingestion runs, source documents, accounts, statement periods,
transactions and adjudications.

Three rules the schema enforces mechanically rather than by convention:

  - Nothing is a float.  Every amount is an integer count of minor units
    in a BigInteger column, paired with an ISO 4217 code.  A test walks
    the metadata and fails on any Float or Numeric column, so the rule
    cannot be broken by a later migration without the suite noticing.

  - Magnitude and sign are separate.  amount_minor is constrained
    non-negative and direction carries credit or debit, so a sign error
    is a rejected row rather than a plausible one.

  - Rows are corrected by supersession, not mutation.  A wrong row is
    marked superseded and points at its replacement, so the record of
    what was originally read survives the correction.

The processor boundary is enforced by the database: transactions carry a
proof_class <> 'p4' check, so an assertion made in unstructured material

Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Add append-only financial ledger schema

The ledger is the system of record for financial evidence.  Six tables:
ingestion runs, source documents, accounts, statement periods,
transactions and adjudications.

Three rules the schema enforces mechanically rather than by convention:

  - Nothing is a float.  Every amount is an integer count of minor units
    in a BigInteger column, paired with an ISO 4217 code.  A test walks
    the metadata and fails on any Float or Numeric column, so the rule
    cannot be broken by a later migration without the suite noticing.

  - Magnitude and sign are separate.  amount_minor is constrained
    non-negative and direction carries credit or debit, so a sign error
    is a rejected row rather than a plausible one.

  - Rows are corrected by supersession, not mutation.  A wrong row is
    marked superseded and points at its replacement, so the record of
    what was originally read survives the correction.

The processor boundary is enforced by the database: transactions carry a
proof_class <> 'p4' check, so an assertion made in unstructured material
can be held as a source document but can never reach the ledger or be
counted in a total.  Adjudications deliberately take no updated_at and

Author: Neil Byrne
Message:
Implement hybrid Vector DB + Neo4j RAG system with debug logging and Show on Graph feature

Major Features:
- Hybrid RAG Architecture: Integrated ChromaDB vector database with Neo4j for optimized context retrieval
  - Vector search for semantic document matching
  - Cypher filtering for graph-based relevance
  - Hybrid filtering combines both approaches for focused context
  - Graceful fallback mechanisms (hybrid -> Cypher-only -> full graph)

- Vector DB Infrastructure:
  - Added VectorDBService (ChromaDB) for document embedding storage
  - Added EmbeddingService supporting OpenAI and Ollama providers
  - Document ingestion pipeline now generates and stores embeddings
  - Backfill script for existing documents

- Debug Logging System:
  - Comprehensive debug log captures all RAG process steps
  - Includes vector search results, Cypher queries, node keys, and final prompts
  - Auto-downloads as markdown file after each AI search
  - Detailed step-by-step visibility into AI assistant operations

- Show on Graph Feature:
  - "Show on Graph" button on AI assistant answers
  - Generates Cypher query from answer summary to extract relevant nodes
  - Automatically creates subgraph with nodes and relationships discussed in answer
  - Uses LLM to infer nodes from answer content rather than text extraction

Backend Changes:
- backend/services/rag_service.py: Major refactor for hybrid filtering, debug logging, and Cypher query generation
- backend/services/llm_service.py: Added answer_question_with_prompt() to return prompts
- backend/services/vector_db_service.py: New ChromaDB service
- backend/services/embedding_service.py: New embedding generation service
- backend/routers/chat.py: Added debug_log and used_node_keys to response, extract-nodes endpoint
- backend/config.py: Added Vector DB configuration options
- ingestion/scripts/ingestion.py: Integrated embedding generation during document ingestion
- ingestion/scripts/neo4j_client.py: Added update_document() method for vector_db_id linking

Frontend Changes:
- frontend/src/components/ChatPanel.jsx: Debug log formatting/download, Show on Graph button
- frontend/src/App.jsx: Added handleShowNodesOnGraph callback for subgraph creation
- frontend/src/services/api.js: Added extractNodesFromAnswer API method

Configuration:
- Added CHROMADB_PATH, EMBEDDING_PROVIDER, EMBEDDING_MODEL config options
- Added VECTOR_SEARCH_ENABLED, VECTOR_SEARCH_TOP_K, HYBRID_FILTERING_ENABLED flags
- Updated requirements.txt with chromadb dependency

Documentation:
- Added VECTOR_DB_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md with detailed implementation plan

This implementation significantly improves LLM context window efficiency by using
semantic search and graph filtering to provide focused, relevant context instead
of the entire graph, reducing token usage and improving answer quality.
